cluster_summary: A set of vulnerabilities where the code fails to verify that the current user has the required access rights (view, edit, admin) before exposing or modifying data, leading to unauthorized access or privilege escalation. The missing checks occur in various contexts: retrieval of documents, revisions, history, listing, and performing state-changing actions like rollback, creation, import, and edits involving sensitive fields.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 3 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Before returning the resource data, call authorizationManager.checkAccess(Right.VIEW, documentReference) and skip or deny access if the check fails. For listings, apply the check to the parent entity (e.g., wiki reference) or to each item as appropriate..

sub_patterns.name: missing per-resource VIEW authorization on data retrieval
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code assumes that query results or retrieved resources are safe to expose without re-verifying the current user's VIEW permission on each specific document, revision, or wiki. This occurs in collection responses, deleted document views, revision access, page history endpoints, page listing, and document title retrieval.
